Heads and Tails

LogicParityInvariants
Game: Pins with a round head and a pointed tail are laid end to end in a ring; at every corner two pins meet in one of three ways. There is nothing to win or lose, but there is a pattern to find.
How to play: Press a pin to turn it round. Tick Hint to count the three kinds of corner, and change the number of pins.

Look for the math

At a corner where two pins meet there are three possibilities: head to head (HH), head to tail (HT) or tail to tail (TT). With three pins, either all the corners are the same or all are different. What happens with more pins?

Three pins

Each pin points either round the triangle or against it. If all three point the same way, every corner is head to tail. Otherwise two agree and one does not, and then there is one corner of each kind. The logic test also went through all eight patterns. With four pins all four corners can be alike, but they can never be all different, since there are only three kinds.

The generalisation: HH = TT

With n pins, the number of head-to-head corners always equals the number of tail-to-tail corners, so HT = n − 2·HH. Why? Start with all pins pointing the same way: HH = TT = 0. Turning one pin round either changes nothing (when the two pins next to it point opposite ways) or changes HH and TT both by 1 in the same direction and HT by 2 the other way (when they point the same way): the page's table. So HH − TT stays 0. The test checked it by trying all 2n patterns for every n from 3 to 20, and the table for every pin of every pattern up to n = 14.

An invariant

This is an invariant: a quantity (HH − TT) that no move can change. Every pattern can be made from the start by turning some of the pins, so it is zero for all of them.

As in the applet, the number of pins runs from 3 to 50, every pin starts pointing the same way, and the counts show only when Hint is ticked; the number is a box here where the applet changes it when you press the number.

Tick Hint and turn pins at random with 8 pins. What do you notice about the numbers of red and blue corners?
